extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for PR practitioners on when to use press releases and how to craft concise, newsworthy releases that communicate a brand's story effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider whether a press release is the right tool
rubrics_metrics.description: In today’s digital environment, there’s a thousand different ways to tell a story and a hundred different platforms, so you really need to consider if the press release is the right tool for the news you’re putting out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate alternative vehicles (guest posts, social media, other platforms) before issuing a release; choose the channel that best fits the news and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sure it’s newsworthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you putting out a new product, launching a new business unit or releasing data? If it is of interest to a large number of people and it’s market moving, you probably have something for a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use press releases for market-moving, broadly interesting items (new products, business unit launches, data releases). If the news is humdrum or not relevant to many people, opt for a guest post or social update instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep brand stories simple and clear / be succinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of our clients serve a variety of vertical industries and may have a lot of products and services—or a very complex technology. The tendency is to go really deep and provide a lot of information, but it is important to keep our brand’s stories simple and clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write compelling messages that succinctly tell a brand’s story; avoid excessive technical depth or unnecessary detail that obscures the main news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure press-release value by distribution and pickup metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Some companies still use them to measure the value of the PR program: how many go out, how many outlets pick them up and how many impressions they get.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track outputs (number distributed), earned media pickup (outlets that publish the release) and impressions as one way to evaluate a release’s reach, while recognizing these are output metrics rather than measures of deeper impact.
